topic_summary: Analysis of Vatican II (1962-1965) as a composite doctrinal shift rather than a single reinterpretation. The council produced 16 documents addressing religious freedom, ecumenism, liturgy, and ecclesiology through negotiated compromise between progressive and conservative factions. Post-conciliar implementation generated competing hermeneutical frameworks (continuity vs. rupture) that read the same conciliar texts as authorizing fundamentally different ecclesiological trajectories.

key_entities: Pope John XXIII (convener; aggiornamento vision; died 1963)
Pope Paul VI (guided council to completion 1963-1965)
Progressive theologians (de Lubac, Congar, Frings; previously censored under Pius XII)
Conservative opposition (Ottaviani, Siri, Ruffini; Coetus Internationalis Patrum)
Conciliar documents (16 total: 4 Constitutions, 9 Decrees, 3 Declarations)
Post-conciliar implementation apparatus (liturgical commissions, episcopal conferences)
Traditionalist rejection movements (claim invalidity due to doctrinal error)
key_tensions: Progressive reform vs. conservative preservation (10-12% rejection votes on key documents)
Doctrinal continuity vs. rupture (hermeneutics debate: Benedict XVI vs. progressive interpreters)
Conciliar text vs. 'spirit of Vatican II' (authorized changes vs. unauthorized experimentation)
Religious freedom innovation vs. prior magisterial teaching (Dignitatis Humanae vs. Syllabus of Errors)
key_mechanisms: Compromise drafting (ambiguous formulations to achieve supermajority votes)
Liturgical reform apparatus (commissions translating Sacrosanctum Concilium into practice)
key_absences: Formal doctrinal adjudication mechanism for resolving hermeneutical disputes
Enforcement structure for distinguishing authorized from unauthorized implementation

readings.commitment: Vatican II is not a single reinterpretation but an overdetermined composite encoding incompatible ecclesiological visions via ambiguous compromise formulations

readings.expected_structural_delta: Conciliar texts simultaneously support continuity and rupture readings because they were designed to achieve supermajority votes by encoding both; hermeneutical control becomes the real locus of authority; implementation divergence is structural feature not bug; 10-12% rejection votes signal unresolved theological incompatibility embedded in final texts

axiom_contradictions.basis: Continuity reading requires that Dignitatis Humanae is reconcilable with Syllabus of Errors (no doctrinal contradiction); rupture reading requires acknowledging the contradiction as doctrinal progress. No single coherent framework can hold both 'DH contradicts prior teaching AND this is legitimate development' and 'DH does not contradict prior teaching because development preserves continuity.'

omegas.description: No formal mechanism exists to adjudicate between continuity and rupture readings. Papal magisterium can assert one reading (Benedict XVI continuity) but cannot compel assent from progressive interpreters who claim equal conciliar authority. The absence of adjudication structure makes hermeneutical control the de facto locus of authority.

If composite overdetermination reading is correct, is the ambiguity stable or does it eventually collapse into one reading? Historical trajectory suggests progressive rupture reading captured implementation apparatus 1965-2005, then partial conservative restoration 2005-2013, then renewed progressive control 2013-present. Stability question remains open.
omegas.source: Composite overdetermination reading + post-conciliar implementation history

omegas.description: What are the structural costs of traditionalist exit (SSPX, sedevacantism)? Does exit reduce or increase pressure on magisterium to resolve hermeneutical ambiguity? Exit may function as safety valve preserving composite stability by removing most committed continuity-reading adherents from institutional contestation.

Sacrosanctum Concilium §36 mandates Latin preservation, yet Latin was nearly eliminated post-1970. Is this unauthorized implementation (continuity reading) or legitimate development (rupture reading)? No enforcement mechanism exists to adjudicate. Composite reading: ambiguity was designed to permit both interpretations.
omegas.source: Deferred axis: liturgical_reform_mechanism + absence of enforcement structure

omegas.description: Does doctrinal development have structural limits, or can any position be reconciled via development? Continuity reading requires limits (DH reconcilable with Syllabus); rupture reading permits contradiction as progress. No agreed criteria exist to distinguish legitimate development from rupture. This is the unresolved theological question Vatican II encoded rather than resolved.
omegas.source: Deferred axis: religious_freedom_doctrinal_shift + axiom contradiction between readings
